subject: ventures/garage-door-bid-calculator
professional: an owner-operator of a small garage-door shop who prices spring and replacement tickets (and a bookkeeper checking the margin-vs-markup arithmetic)

evidence.correctness: Ran calculateBid via /tmp scratch script (scratchpad r.mjs) and recomputed three tickets in a separate Python script using the textbook margin-on-price formula price = cost/(1-margin) with loaded wage = wage*(1+burden). (1) 8x7 spring, $30/h, 30% burden, 1h, 40 mi at 30 mph, $0.70/mi, 15% overhead, 25% margin: tool 328.1333, Python 328.1333, travel share 24.38% both. (2) 16x7 R-9 replacement, 1.5x after-hours, 4.25 h, $2000 proposed: price 3263.8917, $/sqft 29.14, profit 815.97, proposed profit -447.92 both match. (3) explicit driveHours override, 0 margin/overhead: 167.5 both. All match to the cent. Limit: the formula is the author's stated method; I checked arithmetic and the margin-vs-markup convention, not market prices. Starting costs (spring kit $95/$175, $/sqft) were not checked against a supplier price list.
evidence.completeness: Claims checked: job types, size presets, travel from miles/mph, after-hours multiplier on labor only, walk-away price, travelEatsJob flag (spring >=35% or travel > shop labor), proposed-price compare, copy summary, share link, printable proposal (index.html imports proposal.mjs, share.mjs, proposal-terms.mjs, usage.mjs; all exist), niche pages and two vs-pages exist, link to ../bid-price-engine exists. All 8 test files run: 120 tests pass. No TODO/FIXME in code. Did not drive the page in a real browser; page.test.mjs is static. README never mentions the proposal/share/terms features that index.html and 3 modules ship.
evidence.verification: Ran `node --test <file>` for each of 8 test files: calc 15, page 7, proposal-terms 25, proposal 42, share 8, usage 5, vs-spring 9, vs-housecall 9; 0 failures. Mutation 1 in calc.mjs: price = totalCost*(1+margin/100) (markup instead of margin): calc.test.mjs failed 2 (caught). Mutation 2: travelShare >= 35 changed to > 35 on the spring-only flag: 15/15 still pass (NOT caught; the 35% boundary the README advertises is untested). Both reverted; git status clean and 15/15 pass after revert.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs fully. Pure, no DOM, frozen presets, validated numbers with named errors, JSDoc on the input. Defects: derived fields unused/ambiguous (breakEvenPrice duplicates totalCost); an unknown preset throws instead of degrading; a spring-only ticket silently accepts and counts an entered doorCost; width classification single<=10ft is a hard switch (10x8 'single' vs 11ft 'double'), no handling of 2 springs on doubles beyond a flat kit price. Overall acceptable and readable; not read: proposal.mjs/share.mjs internals beyond their passing tests.
evidence.claims: README claims backed: formulas (calc.mjs), 1.3x labor (4.25/3.25 = 1.31, calc.mjs JOB_TYPES), privacy/usage events (usage.mjs, not audited in depth), disclaimer present in README and index.html:289, MIT LICENSE file. Unbacked or stale: llms.txt lists all five pages under duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo, which CLAUDE.md says is only a redirect host now, while README/VENTURE.yaml use marisstella.app; README says 'After using this, you can now quote...' (outcome claim with no usage data, VENTURE.yaml hypotheses all 'untested', stage prototype); README omits proposal/share features that the page and JSON-LD advertise; README 'Limitations' do not mention a proposal feature or the one-spring-kit-per-door simplification. Starting figures are disclaimed as ballpark, which is honest.
evidence.fitness: Walked a shop owner's job: pick job type and size, adjust wage/burden/miles, read price, travel share and walk-away, test a $189 special (case 1 shows $328 needed, travel 24% of price, flagged true because travel $80 > shop labor $39), generate a proposal. Works end to end in the engine. Gap: no sales tax, single currency, no route/multi-door, spring-only labour does not model torsion vs extension (all stated). Real-world usage is unmeasured (VENTURE.yaml usage null), so fitness is judged by walkthrough only.
evidence.domain: A garage-door owner would accept parts + loaded labour + travel + overhead then margin on price (not markup), and charging drive time at loaded wage. Departures: after-hours premium applies only to labor, not to the travel leg of an evening call; overhead is applied on direct cost including parts (some shops apply overhead to labor only); no markup on parts; spring kits priced flat by door class with no cycle-rating or wire-size choice (high-cycle multiplier 1.6 exists as constant); flag for 'walk-away' is break-even cost excluding any margin, which is a defensible but notable definition.

defects.what: Seeded mutation changing the spring travel-share flag from >=35 to >35 passes all 15 calc tests: the headline 35% threshold has no boundary test.
llms.txt links all five pages to the old duncan-haywood.github.io host instead of https://marisstella.app/garage-door-bid-calculator/ used in README and VENTURE.yaml.
README outcome sentence ('After using this, you can now quote...') asserts an effect with no usage evidence; README also omits the shipped proposal, share-link and terms features.
breakEvenPrice is an alias of totalCost; spring-only tickets accept and sum an entered doorCost silently.

verdict: The pricing engine is arithmetically right: three tickets recomputed independently in Python match to the cent, the margin-on-price convention is the correct one, and all 120 tests across 8 files pass. A markup-for-margin mutation was caught, but a boundary change to the headline 35% travel flag was not, so verification sits exactly at the bar. The weakest area is claims: llms.txt points at a retired host, the README carries an unevidenced outcome sentence and omits the proposal/share features, and the starting parts prices are ballpark figures with no sourced check. Starting costs and real-shop usage are unverified (stage prototype, all hypotheses untested). A shop owner could use it for a quote with their own numbers; it meets the numeric bar on correctness and verification but claims scores 2, so it does not meet the bar overall.
